title: SSO/RBAC Contract Matrix & Pricing Experiment Playbook
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Overview:
This ticket defines an experiment and draft playbook for how Redwood will represent SSO/SAML and RBAC commitments in enterprise contracts and packaging. The goal is to create a repeatable pricing matrix and contract language that balances (1) commercial clarity for sales/legal, (2) delivery commitments we can meet operationally, and (3) predictable unit economics for hosted and dedicated customers.

Why now:
- Increasing RFIs show customers treat SSO + scoped RBAC as a gating security requirement.
- Sales cycles elongate when contract commitments are unclear or depend on bespoke engineering work.
- We need a scalable approach across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments.

Success metrics (for experiment):
- <15% increase in average time-to-sign vs baseline for incoming enterprise deals that request SSO/RBAC (target: reduce instead of increase).
- >60% of SSO/RBAC asks covered by standardized contract language and packaging tiers (vs ad-hoc changes).
- Fewer than 3 delivery incidents in first 6 months tied to over-promising RBAC feature scope.
- Sales feedback NPS > 7 on clarity of deliverables in pilot accounts.

Scope / Constraints:
- Focused on SSO (SAML2.0, OIDC) and role-based controls used to scope access to model endpoints, audit logs, and billing data.
- Does NOT include full data residency/legal review for regulated industries (separate stream).
- Applies to Hosted API, Dedicated (reserved GPU pools), and Private (VPC/on-prem) offerings but commitments differ by deployment type.

Proposed Packaging Matrix (summary):
- Enterprise Standard (no additional SLA): SSO via SAML/OIDC; default admin role + basic RBAC (Admin/Developer/Viewer); self-serve onboarding guide; no guaranteed timeline for custom role modeling. Price uplift: +10% on base usage for hosted.
- Enterprise Secure (contracted, 30-day SLA option): SSO via SAML/OIDC with vendor-assisted SSO setup (one onboarding session); defined RBAC scope (Admin, Dev, Billing, ReadOnly, Audit); audit log retention guaranteed for 90 days; includes documented role mapping template. Price uplift: +25% or committed monthly minimum.
- Enterprise Dedicated/Private (deployment-specific commitments): Full SSO integration support, customizable RBAC schema with up to 10 custom roles and up to 5 role-to-route mappings included; on-site or VPC network assistance for Private. Price uplift: custom (reserved capacity contract).

Contract language (examples for legal):
- "Authentication: Vendor shall provide support for SAML 2.0 and OIDC. Vendor will assist Customer with one SSO configuration session and supply configuration documentation. Additional integration assistance will be charged at professional services rates unless otherwise stated in the order form."
- "RBAC Scope: Vendor agrees to provide role-based access controls with the following baseline roles: Admin, Developer, Billing, Viewer, Audit. Any additional custom roles or mapping logic will be scoped as change requests and charged per the agreed professional services rate unless included in the Order Form."
- "Operational Commitments: For contracts that include the Enterprise Secure tier, Vendor will complete SSO onboarding within 30 calendar days of receiving required artifacts from Customer. Failure to meet this timeline will result in a service credit equal to 5% of monthly fees for that billing period, up to a maximum of the monthly recurring charge."

Experiment design and rollout plan:
1) Pilot cohort (Feb–Apr 2025): select 8 inbound enterprise opportunities that requested SSO/RBAC. Offer them one of the three standardized packaging options and track time-to-sign, negotiation points, and delivery effort.
2) Instrumentation: create a simple Jira/Linear label schema and a short intake form for sales to capture requested SSO/RBAC details (protocol, IdP, number of roles, expected user counts, audit log needs).
3) Delivery playbook: engineering and solutions create a "SSO Onboarding Checklist" and an RBAC mapping template. Include templated support PRs and runbook entries.
4) Legal review: submit draft contract language to Legal and Security for review by 2025-02-28 (SEC-209 referenced).
5) Post-pilot decisions (May 2025): decide which packaging options become standard, finalize price uplift ranges, and build any required console UI changes for role templates.

Operational runbook highlights (for Solutions & Support):
- Intake fields required from customer: IdP metadata, SAML endpoints, certificate, expected role definitions, SSO test account credentials.
- Standard test procedure: connect in staging, validate assertions for 3 sample user roles, smoke test access controls to one model endpoint and to billing UI.
- Escalation path: Solutions -> ENG on-call -> Security if assertion validation errors indicate cryptographic issues.

Risk & Trade-offs:
- Over-committing on customizable RBAC will increase engineering maintenance burden and complicate rollout across Dedicated/Private variants. Mitigation: cap included custom roles and route mappings; push advanced customization to Professional Services.
- Pricing unpopular with some buyers who expect SSO for free. Trade-off intentionally prices for operational cost and delivery SLAs; plan to grandfather simple SSO-only requests into Enterprise Standard when volume warrants.
- SLA service credits add accounting complexity; include an option in order forms for customers to opt-out of credits in exchange for higher pricing.

Decision log (selected entries):
- 2025-01-20 — PM sync: agreed to experiment with three-tier packaging rather than single add-on. (Aisha Kapoor, Miguel Ortega, L. Chen)
notes: 2025-01-22: Design asked for UI implications for role templates; created follow-up ENG ticket ENG-8217. 2025-02-05: Legal redline v0.2 uploaded to Drive (https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/SSO-RBAC-DRAFTS). 2025-02-18: Pilot cohort identified (list stored in Confluence). 2025-02-20: Security completed preliminary review; flagged cryptographic test requirements.
